Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

latents 1.4.2

Changes since the CRAN release 1.1.9.

Refit a model made with 1.1.9 if

  • it is a two-step model with covariates and categorical indicators (fixed = "measurement"). Its standard errors now hold the response probabilities, as documented, and can be substantially smaller;
  • you compared a staged fit with a jointly estimated one in compare_models(). Criteria now count the staged fit’s measurement parameters, which can reverse the ranking;
  • you used the local-independence check of diagnostics(). It used unadjusted p-values and flagged a pair in up to half of correctly specified models; it now applies the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment it states;
  • you filtered on p_adjusted from get_results(fit, "residuals"). It was the raw p-value and is now Benjamini-Hochberg, as in get_residuals(); adjust = "none" gives the raw values;
  • it uses grand scaling. The standard deviation is now the population one, weighted by any sampling weights, so likelihoods and scales change slightly;
  • it is an lta() fit with homogeneous transitions and drop_empty = FALSE. Its BIC now counts every row with a positive weight, as the general transition engine’s does.

Warnings

  • A cross-level fit with group classes warns that its likelihood counts the ratings twice, so its criteria favour group classes and the full form even on data with no group structure.
  • Enumerations name the candidates that reached their best log likelihood from one start only; refit those with more n_starts before comparing their criteria.
  • A transition row with fewer than one expected outgoing move warns and is marked unsupported; its Wald tests are refused.
  • descriptives() warns that it describes the recorded rows without weights.

New features

  • One function per plot or table, taking any object the package returns: plot_sizes(), plot_entropy(), plot_posteriors(), plot_avepp(), plot_heatmap(), plot_bars(), plot_raincloud(), plot_parallel(), plot_pairs(), plot_trajectories(), plot_individuals(), plot_classification(), plot_coefficients(), plot_criteria(), plot_deltas(), plot_trust() and plot_all(); get_checks(), get_entropy(), get_classification(), get_avepp(), get_residuals() and get_replication(). overview() prints and draws everything about an object.
  • Enumeration grids have a verb per table (get_candidates(), get_best(), get_deltas(), get_knees(), get_tree()) and print a one-screen summary that warns about edge minima, single-start maxima and low average posteriors.
  • align_labels(fit, reference) numbers one fit’s profiles and group classes like another’s, for comparing samples or waves.
  • profile_covariates and group_covariates work with every covariance structure and take start and fixed; holding the measurement model gives the two-step estimator.
  • three_step() takes a categorical outcome, tests that the classes share one mean or distribution (contrast = "overall"), propagates the measurement model’s uncertainty (step_one = "estimated") and can leave units with a missing outcome out (missing = "exclude").
  • parameter_inference(boundary = "fix"), vcov() and confint() work for lta() fits without covariates, occasion-specific measurement, second order or stayers, and get_results() then reports the standard errors of the means and variances.
  • plot() of a bootstrap from parameter_inference(method = "bootstrap") draws each estimate with its interval; as.data.frame(boot, what = "replicates") returns the replicates.
  • General transition fits have the "posteriors", "entropy" and "information_criteria" tables, and "covariances" with covariance_model = "full".
  • More views of lta() fits: plot_sequences() and plot_profiles() for ordinal, count, weighted and mover-stayer fits; the transition network (get_tna(), get_group_tna()) when transitions are homogeneous and first order; plot_raincloud(), plot_parallel() and plot_pairs() with homogeneous transitions, each answered occasion a case.
  • Fits whose indicators are all ordinal draw plot_profiles() (each profile’s expected category), plot_responses() and plot_heatmap().
  • plot_sequences() sorts the units within each class by their most frequent profile.
  • descriptives() with id reports the within- and between-person standard deviations.
  • plot_individuals() takes persons: how many persons, or which.
  • plot_pairs() marks each profile’s density with its marker, so the curves are told apart by shape as well as colour.
  • Every function has its own help page with a verb-led title; each page lists every argument’s values and default, the fits it accepts and refuses, and the columns it returns.

Bug fixes

  • compare_models(test = "lrt") accepted pairs that are not nested; they are now refused. Comparing shared with group-class slopes failed.
  • lca(count_dispersion = ) fitted the count indicator as Gaussian.
  • confint() failed on a covariate fit with fixed = "measurement".
  • get_results(fit) and as.data.frame(fit) returned an empty profile table for a fit without continuous indicators, lca() fits included; they now return its response table.
  • three_step(): BCH contrasts involving a probability outside [0, 1] were tested; an outcome category seen only on excluded rows removed every categorical ML standard error.
  • mixture_regression() under separation stopped with an error from eigen(); it now returns the fit with NA standard errors and a warning.
  • A bootstrap table whose rows were reordered attached replicates to the wrong parameters; such tables are now refused.
  • Person centring of an indicator observed once in a group fitted artificial zero deviations; it is now refused.
  • Unused factor levels became membership or random-effect parameters.
  • A ragged transition bootstrap crashed; incompatible resamples now count as failures.
  • Weighted fits: some plot subtitles and the posterior-strip means were unweighted, and cross-level prevalence and sample counts included zero-weight groups.
  • diagnostics() reported “2 of 2 starts” for restricted cross-level fits and false thin-profile warnings for constrained covariate fits.
  • predict() ignored a misnamed argument; get_results(pooled, "all") was refused; vcov(pooled, type = ) ignored type.
  • Count-model arguments that do not apply were dropped in silence; they now warn.
  • An invalid option value raises an error that names the argument and its accepted values.
  • Assignment tables lost an identifier column named class; small coefficients lost precision beside large intercepts; regression intercepts were shown as odds or rate ratios.
  • The growth individuals view dropped classes beyond the fourth.
  • plot_sequences() failed on an occasion no group answered.
  • plot_parallel() bridged a missing middle indicator and did not draw a case with one answered value between gaps.
  • plot_all() of an ordinal lta() fit failed.
  • Plot legends left out the key of a status no candidate had.
  • A platform that does not report its processor count failed in fork(); it now runs on one core with a warning.

latents 1.1.9

CRAN release: 2026-11-01

Changes since the CRAN release 0.9.21.

Refit a model made with 0.9.21 if

  • its Gaussian indicators are recorded in small units (proportions, metres, rates). The variance floor and the EM stopping rule now do not depend on the units, and fits in small units can reach a much higher likelihood;
  • its occasions are labelled T1 … T10. They were ordered alphabetically; such labels are now refused, so give the order with factor(levels = );
  • it uses sampling weights with zeros. Units of weight zero now count for nothing;
  • it has several group classes. The classes may now be numbered the other way round, with the same estimates;
  • it is an EII, EEI or EEE model, which now defaults to search = "emEM" and can reach a higher maximum (search = "kmeans" gives the old fit);
  • you compared models on ICL, AWE or CLC, which now use the entropy of the complete classification.

New features

  • compare_models(..., test = "lrt") tests each nested model against the one before it.
  • get_results(grid, "lmr"): Vuong-Lo-Mendell-Rubin and adjusted Lo-Mendell-Rubin tests.
  • local_dependence = "item1:item2" models a pair of indicators jointly within each class.
  • direct_effects = "y ~ z" lets a covariate shift an indicator’s mean in every profile.
  • three_step(method = "ml") for distal outcomes, and r3step() on lta() fits.
  • predict() for growth mixtures.
  • diagnostics() reports estimation, class sizes, classification, local independence and information, one row per quantity.
  • print() says how many starts reached the best log likelihood.
  • cores runs the starts of one fit, an enumeration or sensitivity() in parallel, with the same result as one core.
  • New arguments: scaling (grand or within-person z-scores), boundary = "exclude" (set aside starts with a variance at its bound) and drop_empty (rows with no observed indicator).
  • New and extended plots: plot_sequences(), plot_selection(), more views in plot_profiles(), group-level views in plot_diagnostics(), and one plot per tree in plot_tree() (combine = TRUE for one panel).

Bug fixes

  • coef() of some lta() fits returned centred means.
  • sensitivity(fit, data = ) dropped every seed for single-level fits.
  • Rows with no observed indicator were assigned a class and counted in the classification error and three-step estimates.
  • mixture_regression(common = "intercept") had no effect; it is now refused.

latents 0.9.21

CRAN release: 2026-10-16
